newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa may net under $200 mln for cable stake.
newsitem.headline: Televisa may net under $200 mln for cable stake.

text.p: Mexican media group Grupo Televisa may net less than $200 million for the sale of its remaining 51 percent stake in cable television unit Cablevision, Televisa vicepresident Guillermo Canedo White said in a telephone interview.

The sale of the stake "will be more or less in the terms of the previous operation, but it will be necessary to discount the value of the frequencies we are keeping," Canedo told Reuters. "The frequencies could be worth about $20 million, more or less."
He was referring to the sale of 49 percent of Cablevision to Sercotel, a subsidiary of phone giant Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), carried out July 5 1995 for $211 million.

Canedo said that a proposal put to Mexico's Federal Monopolies Commission (CFC) concerning selling its remaining stake in Cablevision to Telmex includes breaking out two Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, to be retained by Televisa.
"Of course, when the sell-off plan was drawn up it was always said that the bands would stay with us because they are considered strategic for us," Canedo said.

Cablevision was notified by the government in 1994 that it would be authorized to operate the two UHF-band concessions, but the assignation process was suspended when rival cable firm Multivision took court action over the award.
Canedo said Televisa was confident it would win the court case. Multivision officials were not available to comment.
"There is a whole legal process which makes us think we have rights to them (the concessions) way beyond the radio spectrum auction," he said.

The government intends to auction off concessions to operate telecommunications services in slices of the radio spectrum, including UHF frequencies, but has not said whether it will recognize concessions already given out such as the ones Televisa claims.
In the Televisa document sent to the CFC, the company acknowledged a market share of 64.21 percent for Multivision in pay TV in Mexico City, compared to 35.79 percent for Cablevision.
